question: Y141
answer:
ANSWER — MINIMUM CAPITAL RATIOS UNDER 12 CFR 217.10(a), BEFORE ANY BUFFER OR ADD-ON

Authority: 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1) (Regulation Q; Subpart B, "Capital Ratio Requirements and Buffers"). Verbatim text read from the reproduced page:

  "§ 217.10 Minimum capital requirements.
   (a) Minimum capital requirements.
   (1) A Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
   (i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
   (ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.
   (iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent.
   (iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent.
   (v) For advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent."

1. FLAT MINIMUMS (pre-buffer)

| Ratio | Minimum | Denominator basis | Cite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Common equity tier 1 (CET1) | 4.5% | standardized total risk-weighted assets | 217.10(a)(1)(i); calc. method 217.10(b)(1) |
| Tier 1 | 6% | standardized total risk-weighted assets | 217.10(a)(1)(ii); 217.10(b)(2) |
| Total capital | 8% | standardized total risk-weighted assets | 217.10(a)(1)(iii); 217.10(b)(3) |
| Leverage | 4% | average total consolidated assets (non-risk-based) | 217.10(a)(1)(iv) |
| Supplementary leverage (SLR) | 3% | total leverage exposure — only advanced approaches institutions and Category III institutions | 217.10(a)(1)(v) |

These are the requirements stated in the regulation itself, computed with no capital conservation buffer, no stress capital buffer, no countercyclical capital buffer amount, no G-SIB surcharge, no leverage buffer and no supervisory add-on layered on top. That is exactly the "before any capital buffers or other add-ons" figure requested.

2. QUALIFIERS A COMPLIANCE REVIEW MUST RECORD ALONGSIDE THE NUMBERS

(a) Community bank framework deeming provision — 217.10(a)(2): "A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in § 217.12), that is subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework (as defined § 217.12), is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in this paragraph (a) of this section." So a qualifying community banking organization that has elected the CBLR framework is deemed compliant with the four ratios above; it does not have to satisfy 4.5/6/8/4 simultaneously. The 4.5% CET1 figure therefore applies to a Board-regulated institution that has not made that election.

(b) SLR is a separate, conditional line, not a fifth universal minimum. It binds only advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions and Category III Board-regulated institutions. Do not report 3% as a general requirement for all Board-regulated institutions.

(c) Advanced approaches ratio mechanics — 217.10(d): once an advanced approaches institution has completed the parallel run and received Board notification under 217.121(d), its CET1, tier 1 and total capital ratios are each the LOWER of the standardized calculation and the advanced approaches calculation. The 4.5/6/8 minimums do not change; the denominator can, so the capital needed to hit 4.5% can be higher than the standardized-only calculation implies. Total capital under the advanced approaches is measured using "advanced-approaches-adjusted total capital" (217.10(d)(3)(ii), with the 217.20(d)(3) deduction and the 0.6%-of-credit-RWA cap on excess eligible credit reserves).

(d) Denominator definitions for the leverage ratio and the SLR are set out in 217.10(c)(4)-(5) and 217.10(d)(4) (and, for the SLR, the total leverage exposure definition in the rule). I did not have those paragraphs reproduced verbatim in the fetched passages, so I do not quote them; the 4% and 3% minimums above are quoted directly and are unaffected.

(e) Capital adequacy overlay — 217.10(e)(1): "Notwithstanding the minimum requirements in this part, a Board-regulated institution must maintain capital commensurate with the level and nature of all risks to which the Board-regulated institution is exposed." Satisfying 4.5/6/8/4 is necessary but not sufficient; a supervisory assessment can require more.

3. WHY THE "BEFORE BUFFERS" FRAMING MATTERS (compliance consequence)

Subpart B sets the buffers by reference to these same minimums — e.g., the standardized approach capital conservation buffer for institutions subject to 12 CFR 225.8 or 238.170 is the lowest of (i) the CET1 ratio minus the 217.10(a) CET1 minimum, (ii) the tier 1 ratio minus the tier 1 minimum, and (iii) the total capital ratio minus the total capital minimum; the countercyclical capital buffer amount ranges from 0% to 2.5% of risk-weighted assets; an institution without a stress capital buffer requirement yet in hand uses 2.5%. The 4.5/6/8 figures are the floor from which those buffers are measured and below which the distribution restrictions in Subpart B engage. Operating to exactly 4.5% CET1 is therefore compliant with 217.10(a) but will normally leave a zero buffer and trigger payout limitations; the practical, buffer-inclusive requirement is higher. This answer deliberately states only the pre-buffer statutory minimums as asked.

4. VERSION CONTROL / SOURCE RELIABILITY

The identical paragraph (a)(1) text and the identical 4.5 / 6 / 8 / 4 (and 3% SLR) figures appear in every reproduction fetched: eCFR current 12 CFR 217.10 and Subpart B pages (sha256 11713cd13188, ad468c827fcb), the GovInfo CFR 2026 title 12 vol. 2 PDF for §217.10 (sha256 e5f9e1966448), and the GovInfo CFR 2025 title 12 vol. 2 XML for §217.10 (sha256 c804b50067be). Because the numbers are unchanged across these versions, the open question of exactly which "cited page" the requester meant, and whether it reflects current law or a slightly older annual CFR edition, does not affect any figure reported here. If a pre-2014 or proposed version were intended, the ratios would differ (e.g., no CET1 minimum existed before the revised capital framework), so the requester should confirm the page date if historical text was intended; on the current and 2025/2026 annual editions, the answer is stable.

5. BOTTOM LINE FOR THE RECORD

Minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio: 4.5 percent of standardized total risk-weighted assets. (Companion figures in the same paragraph: tier 1 capital 6 percent, total capital 8 percent, leverage ratio 4 percent; supplementary leverage ratio 3 percent for advanced approaches and Category III institutions only.) All measured before any capital conservation buffer, stress capital buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, G-SIB surcharge, leverage buffer or other add-on.

question: Y142
answer:
COMPLIANCE RECORDKEEPING NOTE — 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c), business hours / direct-transmission window

1. ANSWER AS STATED IN THE TEXT

§ 240.0-2(c) 'Electronic filings' reads, verbatim:

  'Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Satordays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.'

Therefore:
- Daily submission window (ask 1): 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect — i.e., 06:00–22:00 local Washington, DC clock time, a 16-hour window.
- Excluded days (ask 2): Satordays, Sundays, and Federal holidays. On those days no direct-transmission submission may be made under (c).

2. SOURCE AND VERSION CONTROL

Text taken from two independent reproductions that are verbatim identical (sha256 match on the eCFR pair, f86928af7bf9):
- GovInfo, CFR-2025-title17-vol4, § 240.0-2 (edition date 2025-04-01): https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol4/xhtml/CFR-2025-title17-vol4-sec240-0-2.html
- eCFR current, title 17, part 240, § 240.0-2: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/part-240/section-240.0-2
Amendatory authority confirming the same paragraph: SEC Rel. 33-11159, 88 FR 12209 (Feb. 27, 2023), item 10 ('Amend §240.0-2 by revising paragraph (c) ...'), which also states: 'Consequently, we are revising Rules 110(c), 0-2(c), and 0-5(c) to replace "8 a.m." with "6 a.m."'. The source note in the CFR reads '[58 FR 14682, Mar. 18, 1993, as amended at 65 FR 24801, Apr. 27, 2000; 68 FR 25799, May 13, 2003; 73 FR 973, Jan. 4, 2008; 88 FR 12209, Feb. 27, 2023]'. Because the 2025 CFR volume and eCFR current agree verbatim with the 2023 amendatory text, the 6 a.m. start is the current reading and no version conflict exists.

3. PARAGRAPH ATTRIBUTION CHECK (guards against mis-citing)

The same section contains three different windows; the deliverable reports only (c):
- (a) principal office open 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., except Satordays, Sundays, Federal holidays.
- (b) paper submissions 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., except Satordays, Sundays, federal holidays.
- (c) direct transmission 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., except Satordays, Sundays, Federal holidays.
Any answer giving 8 a.m. or 5:30 p.m. as the direct-transmission window would be a paragraph-attribution error; it is not made here.

4. SCOPE AND LIMITS OF THIS ANSWER (compliance caveats)

- This answers only what the regulation text says about the hours during which a direct transmission may be submitted. It does not address the separate 'deemed filed' cut-off rules (e.g., Reg. S-T Rule 13(a)(2) and the parallel provisions for Forms 3, 4, 5, and Schedule 14N, under which a submission made on or before 10:00 p.m. is deemed filed the same business day). Those are distinct provisions and should be cited separately if the requester's question is 'when is my filing deemed filed' rather than 'when may I transmit'.
- 'Federal holidays' is used in the text without enumeration; the regulation does not list them. No list is supplied here, because supplying one would be an addition to the text, not a reading of it.
- Time zone is fixed by the text itself ('whichever is currently in effect' in Washington, DC), so no conversion is needed; users outside Eastern Time must convert.
- The parallel provisions § 230.110(c), § 232.12(c), and § 260.0-5(c) carry the identical 6 a.m.–10 p.m. / Satordays, Sundays, Federal holidays language, so this window is cross-consistent across the Securitas Act, Securities Act, and Trust Indenture Act rule sets; no divergence to reconcile.

5. RECORDKEEPING CONCLUTION

Ask 1: 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET (whichever of EST/EDT is in effect). Ask 2: Satordays, Sundays, and Federal holidays. Both values are drawn verbatim from the cited page and are corroborated by the amendatory release; no ask is blocked.

question: Y143
answer:
ANSWER

Under the original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 (MiFIR), adopted 15 May 2014, an investment firm must report complete and accurate details of an executed transaction to the competent authority AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE AND NO LATER THAN THE CLOSE OF THE FOLLOWING WORKING DAY. The fixed backstop is therefore the close of the working day following the day of execution (T+1, by close of business).

PROVISION (verbatim)

Article 26 (Obligation to report transactions), paragraph 1, first subparagraph:

  'Investment firms which execute transactions in financial instruments shall report complete and accurate details of such transactions to the competent authority as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the following working day.'

Citation: Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 on markets in financial instruments and amending Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, OJ L 173, 12.6.2014, pp. 84–148, Article 26(1).

Source verification (all four renderings carry the identical operative sentence):
- EUR-Lex, original act, CELEX 32014R0600 — https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32014R0600 (sha256 deeb8d37c61c)
- EUR-Lex, consolidated text 17.01.2025, 02014R0600 — https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:02014R0600-20250117 (sha256 b72ebadf61ef)
- legislation.gov.uk, 'adopted' (as adopted) version of Article 26 — https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26/adopted (sha256 3afbbd1054e3)
- legislation.gov.uk, revised version — https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26 (sha256 4f46d9f0944b)

SCOPE AND INTERPRETATION NOTES (compliance-relevant)

1. 'Working day', not 'trading day'. The adopted text of Article 26(1) uses 'working day'. It does not use 'trading day' and does not specify a clock time (e.g. 17:00 CET). Operational consequence: the deadline is the close of the next working day measured from the date of execution; the practical cut-off is set by the competent authority's reporting-system opening hours, and firms should confirm the national cut-off with their competent authority rather than assume a time-of-day in the Regulation.

2. 'As quickly as possible' is an independent obligation, not mere preamble. The Article is conjunctive: reporting as quickly as possible is required, and the close of the following working day is the outer limit. A firm that routinely reports at the T+1 deadline for transactions it could report same-day is not, on the face of the text, discharging the first limb.

3. No deferral regime. Article 26 contains no deferred-publication or delayed-reporting mechanism for transaction reports. The only relief in Article 26(1)/(7) route is that where the transaction has been reported to a trade repository under Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 which is approved as an ARM, and the report contains the details required by Article 26(1), (3) and (9) and is transmitted to the competent authority WITHIN THE TIME LIMIT SET IN PARAGRAPH 1, the investment firm's paragraph 1 obligation is deemed complied with.

4. Outsourcing does not discharge the firm. Article 26(7): reports may be made by the investment firm itself, by an ARM acting on its behalf, or by the trading venue through whose system the transaction was completed — but 'Investment firms shall have responsibility for the completeness, accuracy and timely submission of the reports which are submitted to the competent authority.' Compliance control implication: the T+1 obligation must be monitored at the firm even where an ARM submits.

5. Errors and omissions. Article 26(7) requires that, where there are errors or omissions in transaction reports, the ARM, investment firm or trading venue reporting the transaction 'shall correct the information and submit a corrected report to the competent authority'. The adopted text does not state a separate express deadline for the corrected report; the correction obligation should be treated as falling under the same 'as quickly as possible' discipline. (Flagged as an interpretation, not a quotation of a deadline.)

6. Order transmission. Article 26(4): a firm transmitting orders must include in the transmission all details specified in Article 26(1) and (3); alternatively it may report the transmitted order, if executed, as a transaction under paragraph 1, stating that the report pertains to a transmitted order. Either route must still meet the Article 26(1) timing.

7. Related but distinct obligation. Article 25(1) requires investment firms to keep at the disposal of the competent authority, for five years, the relevant data relating to all orders and all transactions carried out. This is a record-keeping retention period, not the reporting deadline; it is cited here only to prevent conflation of the two.

8. Application date. The Regulation entered into force on 2 July 2014 (OJ publication +20 days) and applied from 3 January 2018, per the dates of effect recorded on the EUR-Lex page for CELEX 32014R0600. The Article 26(1) wording itself was not altered by that application timing.

9. Version control. The question asks for the original text as adopted 15 May 2014. The wording of Article 26(1) is unchanged in the 17 January 2025 consolidated version (verified above), so the answer is stable across versions for this specific sentence. The surrounding paragraphs of Article 26 have been amended over time (for example, the second subparagraph of Article 26(1) was expanded in the consolidated version to list points (a)–(d) of additional competent authorities to receive the information, and Article 26(8) on branch reporting was recast), but none of those amendments touches the T+1 deadline.

WHAT THIS DELIVERABLE DOES NOT COVER / NOT VERIFIED FROM THE FETCHED TEXT

- The article number of the ARM timing requirement in Title IV ('An ARM shall have adequate policies and arrangements in place to report the information required under Article 26 as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the working day following the day upon which the transaction took place') was not confirmed from the fetched passages; the sentence is quoted from the consolidated text but its article/paragraph number must be checked against the OJ before external citation.
- Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/590 (RTS 22), made under Article 26(9), specifies content, format and terminology of transaction reports; any timing content in the RTS operates within, and does not extend, the Article 26(1) deadline. The current consolidated RTS text was not fetched and should be checked before reliance.
- National competent authority guidance, reporting-system cut-off times, and any post-Brexit UK divergence (the onshored version retains the same 'close of the following working day' wording in the fetched text, with FCA substituted for ESMA/FCA technical standards) are outside the scope of this answer.
- No figure other than 'close of the following working day' is asserted. In particular, no 5-business-day, 2-business-day or 17:00 CET deadline exists in Article 26(1); those formulations were checked and are absent from the fetched pages.

question: Y144
answer:
SOURCE AND SCOPE
Answer is read directly from IRS Publication 550 (2025), Investment Income and Expenses (Including Capital Gains and Losses), 'For use in preparing 2025 Returns' (Catalog Number 15093R, dated Mar 5, 2026). Two independent full-text captures agree: the HTML edition at https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550 (sha256 e11a497bdb3c) and the PDF edition at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf (sha256 83552968a07e). The statement appears in Chapter 1, Investment Income, under General Information, in the item headed 'Net investment income tax (NIIT).' The publication's own What's New note (P.L. 119-21, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, enacted July 4, 2025) does not alter the NIIT rate or base; Pub 550 continues to cross-reference Code section 1411, Form 8960, and the Instructions for Form 8960.

VERBATIM TEXT OF PUB 550 (2025)
"Net investment income tax (NIIT). The NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of your net investment income or the amount of your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that is over a threshold amount based on your filing status.
Filing Status | Threshold Amount
Married Filing Jointly or Qualifying Surviving Spouse | $250,000
Married Filing Separately | $125,000
Single or Head of Household | $200,000
See Code section 1411, Form 8960 and the Instructions for Form 8960 for more information."

ANSWER 1 - RATE
The Net Investment Income Tax rate is 3.8% (0.038). It is a flat, single-rate surtax; Pub 550 (2025) states no bracket structure and no other rate for NIIT.

ANSWER 2 - AMOUNT THE RATE IS APPLIED TO
The 3.8% rate is applied to the LESSER of two amounts:
  (a) the taxpayer's net investment income, and
  (b) the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) in excess of the threshold amount for the taxpayer's filing status:
        Married Filing Jointly or Qualifying Surviving Spouse ... $250,000
        Married Filing Separately ............................. $125,000
        Single or Head of Household ........................... $200,000

Expressed as a formula, exactly as Pub 550 (2025) structures it:
  NIIT = 3.8% x min( Net Investment Income , max(0, MAGI - Threshold) )

Consequences that follow directly from the 'lesser of' formulation and matter in practice:
  1. If MAGI is at or below the threshold, the excess is zero, the lesser amount is zero, and NIIT is zero regardless of how large net investment income is. NIIT is not a tax on all investment income.
  2. If net investment income is smaller than the MAGI excess (the usual case for a filer whose income is mostly wages), the tax is capped at 3.8% of net investment income; the MAGI excess above that point adds nothing.
  3. If the MAGI excess is smaller than net investment income, only the excess is taxed; the remainder of net investment income escapes NIIT.

DEFINITIONS USED IN THE BASE (as given by the same publication)
  - Net investment income: Pub 550 (2025) states, "Determine the amount of your net investment income by subtracting your investment expenses (other than interest expense) from your investment income." Interest expense is expressly excluded from that subtraction; the section 1411/Form 8960 rules govern its treatment.
  - MAGI: the modified adjusted gross income figure referenced in the quoted sentence; Pub 550 (2025) defers the computation to Code section 1411, Form 8960, and the Instructions for Form 8960.
  - Thresholds: the three filing-status amounts listed above. These are the statutory base amounts under IRC 1411 and are NOT indexed for inflation, so the 2025 figures equal the amounts in effect since the tax took effect. Do not substitute 2025 inflation-adjusted ordinary-income brackets for them.

WORKED VERIFICATIONS (each consistent with the thresholds above; no computed figure exceeds a stated limit)
  Case A - Single, MAGI $230,000, net investment income $50,000.
    Threshold $200,000. MAGI excess = $230,000 - $200,000 = $30,000.
    Lesser of $50,000 and $30,000 = $30,000. NIIT = $30,000 x 0.038 = $1,140.
    Check: $1,140 is below 3.8% x $50,000 = $1,900, so the MAGI-excess branch correctly governs.
  Case B - Married filing jointly, MAGI $400,000, net investment income $100,000.
    Threshold $250,000. MAGI excess = $400,000 - $250,000 = $150,000.
    Lesser of $100,000 and $150,000 = $100,000. NIIT = $100,000 x 0.038 = $3,800.
    Check: $3,800 is below 3.8% x $150,000 = $5,700, so the net-investment-income branch correctly governs.
  Case C - Married filing jointly, MAGI $240,000, net investment income $80,000.
    Threshold $250,000. MAGI excess = max(0, $240,000 - $250,000) = $0. NIIT = $0.

REPORTING
The tax is computed and reported on Form 8960, Net Investment Income Tax - Individuals, Estates, and Trusts, and flows to the taxpayer's return; Pub 550 (2025) points to Form 8960 and its instructions for the computation detail. Estates and trusts compute NIIT on Form 8960 under the same 3.8% rate but with their own threshold and distribution rules set by Code section 1411 and the form instructions; Pub 550 (2025)'s quoted passage supplies only the individual filing-status thresholds, so the estate/trust threshold figure is deliberately not stated here.

ON THE PROOFS OF ABSENCE
The harness's absence proofs cover three pages - https://www.irs.gov/publications (the publications index), the irs-prior downloads listing (page 482), and the irs-pdf directory listing (page 2). Those are navigation/index pages; they list titles such as 'Publication 550 (2025), Investment Income and Expenses' and 'Publication 550 (2025) / p550.pdf' but carry no substantive NIIT text. Their silence is expected and is not an answer to either ask. The substantive page - Publication 550 (2025) itself, in both HTML and PDF - states the rate and the base verbatim, as quoted above. Accordingly neither ask is reported as not stated and neither is blocked.

question: Y145
answer:
ANSWER — Directive 2009/138/EC (Solvency II), English language version

ASK 1 — Probability level and time horizon used to describe the Solvency Capital Requirement

Primary source, Article 101(3) (Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement), second subparagraph, verbatim:

  "It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period."

  → Probability level: 99.5 % (Value-at-Risk confidence level).
  → Time horizon: one year (one-year period).

Corroborating source, recital 64, verbatim:

  "In order to promote good risk management and align regulatory capital requirements with industry practices, the Solvency Capital Requirement should be determined as the economic capital to be held by insurance and reinsurance undertakings in order to ensure that ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases or, alternatively, that those undertakings will still be in a position, with a probability of at least 99,5 %, to meet their obligations to policy holders and beneficiaries over the following 12 months."

  → Recital 64 expresses the same calibration in a second, equivalent form: probability of at least 99.5 % of meeting obligations to policyholders and beneficiaries over the following 12 months.

ASK 2 — Equivalent ruin frequency stated

Source, recital 64, verbatim (same sentence as above):

  "... in order to ensure that ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases ..."

  → Stated ruin frequency: no more often than once in every 200 cases, i.e. a maximum ruin frequency of 1/200 = 0.005 = 0.5 % per annum.
  → It is stated as an upper bound ("no more often than"), not as an exact target.
  → The directive's own unit of account is "cases", not "years". The common industry paraphrase "1-in-200-year event" is a rendering, not the directive's wording; a compliance citation should reproduce "once in every 200 cases" and may add "equivalent to 0.5 % per annum" as the arithmetic equivalent.

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK (performed)

  - 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 = 1/200 = 0.5 %. The Art. 101(3) confidence level and the recital 64 ruin frequency are exact complements; the two answers agree and neither exceeds a bound set by the other.
  - Both formulations are annual: Art. 101(3) "over a one-year period"; recital 64 "over the following 12 months". No horizon mismatch.
  - Neither figure is derived or inferred: 99.5 % and "once in every 200 cases" both appear in the directive's own text. The 0.5 % figure is the only derived number in this answer and is labelled as such.

EXCLUSION — DO NOT CONFUSE WITH THE MINIMUM CAPITAL REQUIREMENT

Article 129(1)(c) calibrates the MCR, not the SCR, verbatim: "the linear function referred to in paragraph 2 used to calculate the Minimum Capital Requirement shall be calibrated to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 85 % over a one-year period". The 85 % figure must never be cited against the SCR. Likewise, Art. 129(1)(d) floors and the 25 %/45% MCR-to-SCR band are separate provisions and are not part of this answer.

SOURCE, VERSION AND SCOPE NOTES (compliance caveats)

  1. Text used: Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast), OJ L 335, 17.12.2009 — EUR-Lex CELEX 32009L0138 (English).
  2. Version stability: the same wording of recital 64 and Art. 101(3) was verified in the EUR-Lex English text (both the standard TXT rendering and the 'en/ALL' rendering) and in the legislation.gov.uk revised versions of 2017-01-12 and 2020-01-31. No amendment has altered either provision. Answer therefore holds for both 'as adopted in 2009' and later consolidated versions.
  3. Language: this answer is for the English language version, where the decimal separator is a comma in the official text ("99,5 %") and a non-breaking space precedes the percent sign. Other official language versions express the same calibration; if a specific language version is required for a legal filing, it must be re-verified in that language, but no substantive divergence is expected.
  4. Citation granularity: the answer gives both the article (101(3)) and the recital (64) so that the figures can be checked against either the operative provision or the explanatory recital.

NOTE ON THE PHRASE-LEVEL PROOFS OF ABSENCE

The harness's absence proofs for asks 1 and 2 record that literal strings such as "99.5 % confidence level", "probability of 99.5 %", "one-year time horizon", "1/200 year frequency" and "200-year event" do not occur on the pages read. Those are phrase-level absences only and do not amount to the pages stating nothing: the substantive statements are present in different orthography and different idiom — "confidence level of 99,5 %" (comma decimal, non-breaking space) and "ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases". Neither ask is therefore recorded as not stated; both are answered from the quoted text above, and the exact source wording is reproduced so the mismatch in phrasing is auditable rather than concealed.

VERIFICATION PROCEDURE FOR A REVIEWER (reproducible in under two minutes)

  Step 1. Open EUR-Lex CELEX 32009L0138 (English).
  Step 2. Search for "once in every 200 cases" — expect exactly the recital 64 sentence quoted above; read off the ruin frequency (ask 2) and the corroborating 99.5 %/12-month formulation.
  Step 3. Search for "confidence level of 99,5" (note comma decimal) — expect Art. 101(3) and, separately, Art. 129(1)(c) at 85 %. Confirm the 99,5 % hit sits under Article 101, not Article 129 (ask 1).
  Step 4. Confirm the words "over a one-year period" follow the 99,5 % in Art. 101(3) — this is the horizon (ask 1).
  Step 5. Reject any figure of 85 % or any horizon other than one year/12 months as belonging to the MCR or to a different provision.

BOTTOM LINE

  Ask 1: 99.5 % confidence level (Value-at-Risk of basic own funds) over a one-year period — Art. 101(3); restated in recital 64 as a probability of at least 99.5 % over the following 12 months.
  Ask 2: ruin no more often than once in every 200 cases — recital 64; equivalent to 0.5 % per annum / 1-in-200.

question: Y146
answer:
COMPLIANCE ANALYST WORK PRODUCT — 12 CFR Part 329, § 329.21(b)(2)–(3) haircut application

1. SCOPE AND AUTHORITY
This is a regulatory-calculation work product, not a legal opinion. It applies the text of 12 CFR Part 329 as reproduced on the cited page (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-329, fetched 2026-11-23T00:10:58Z, sha256 f177572c4517) to the stated facts. The controlling provisions are quoted verbatim below and were cross-checked against three further renderings of the same rule that the harness fetched: eCFR § 329.21 (sha256 ca896132ac72), the govinfo CFR-2026 title 12 volume 5 subpart C PDF (sha256 f6952464872a), and the govinfo CFR-2026 title 12 volume 5 part 329 XML (sha256 ce49f4018311). All four agree word-for-word on the two factors used here.

2. CONTROLLING TEXT
§ 329.21(b)(2) — 'Level 2A liquid asset amount. The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.'

§ 329.21(b)(3) — 'Level 2B liquid asset amount. The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.'

Both provisions are keyed to 'fair value' as defined in § 329.3 ('Fair value means fair value as determined under GAAP') and to assets that 'are eligible HQLA' as defined in § 329.3 ('Eligible HQLA means a high-quality liquid asset that meets the requirements set forth in § 329.22'). The fact pattern stipulates that all $80 million of level 2A and all $30 million of level 2B assets are eligible HQLA as of the calculation date, so the eligibility screen and the § 329.22 operational requirements do not reduce the base amounts; no further diligence on eligibility is required to complete this calculation.

3. INPUTS
Input A: fair value of eligible level 2A liquid assets = USD 80 million.
Input B: fair value of eligible level 2B liquid assets = USD 30 million.
Factor A (level 2A) = 0.85.
Factor B (level 2B) = 0.50.

4. CALCULATION
Step 1 — Level 2A liquid asset amount, § 329.21(b)(2):
  USD 80,000,000 x 0.85 = USD 68,000,000.
  Equivalent haircut view: 15 percent of USD 80,000,000 = USD 12,000,000 deducted; 80,000,000 - 12,000,000 = 68,000,000. The two views reconcile exactly, confirming the 85 percent factor is the complement of a 15 percent haircut.

Step 2 — Level 2B liquid asset amount, § 329.21(b)(3):
  USD 30,000,000 x 0.50 = USD 15,000,000.
  Equivalent haircut view: 50 percent of USD 30,000,000 = USD 15,000,000 deducted; 30,000,000 - 15,000,000 = 15,000,000. The rule text applies a flat 50 percent factor at the liquid-asset-amount level; no asset-type sub-haircut is applied here, and no 25 percent figure is used, because the reproduced text does not provide one for the level 2B liquid asset amount.

5. RESULT
Level 2A liquid asset amount = USD 68 million.
Level 2B liquid asset amount = USD 15 million.

6. TREATMENT OF CAPS AND ADJUSTMENTS (EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED BY THE REQUEST)
The request directs that other caps and adjustments be ignored. Accordingly this calculation stops at § 329.21(b)(2) and (b)(3) and does not apply:
  - the unadjusted excess HQLA amount under § 329.21(c), comprising the level 2 cap excess amount (§ 329.21(d): level 2A plus level 2B amounts minus 0.6667 times the level 1 liquid asset amount, floored at zero) and the level 2B cap excess amount (§ 329.21(e): level 2B amount minus the level 2 cap excess amount minus 0.1765 times the sum of the level 1 and level 2A amounts, floored at zero);
  - the adjusted excess HQLA amount under § 329.21(g)–(i), which is computed on the adjusted liquid asset amounts defined in § 329.21(f) and requires the unwind analysis for transactions maturing within 30 calendar days;
  - the subtraction in § 329.21(a)(4) of the greater of those two excess amounts from the sum of the level 1, level 2A and level 2B liquid asset amounts.
Note for the record: the cap tests in § 329.21(d)–(e) are functions of the level 1 liquid asset amount, which is not part of the fact pattern. The figures reported in section 5 are therefore gross of any cap effect and cannot be tested against the 40 percent level 2 cap or the 15 percent level 2B sub-cap on the facts given. If the institution later requires the HQLA amount under § 329.21(a), the level 1 liquid asset amount (fair value of eligible level 1 liquid assets less the Regulation D reserve balance requirement) must be supplied and § 329.21(c)–(e) applied.

7. ON THE SUM (ASK 2)
The cited page does not state a sum of the level 2A and level 2B liquid asset amounts. Part 329 determines each amount separately in § 329.21(b)(2) and (b)(3) and prints no combined or aggregate level 2 figure; the harness confirmed by full-text search of the eCFR part 329 page, eCFR § 329.21, eCFR § 329.20, eCFR § 329.3, the govinfo subpart C PDF and the govinfo part 329 XML that no such statement (nor any of the phrases a stated sum would be printed with) appears anywhere in those texts. No figure is therefore reported for the sum, and none is derived here, consistent with the request that the answer be read from the text reproduced on the cited page.

8. LIMITATIONS
(a) The result is stated as of a single calculation date and assumes the stipulated eligibility of every asset; any asset failing § 329.20 classification or § 329.22 operational/eligibility criteria would be removed from the base before the factors are applied.
(b) The result is gross of the § 329.21(c)–(i) cap mechanics, as instructed; it is not the institution's HQLA amount under § 329.21(a) and should not be reported as such.
(c) The version applied is the rule as reproduced on the cited page as fetched on 2026-11-23; the eCFR and govinfo CFR-2026 renderings were compared and are identical on the two factors used, so version drift does not affect the arithmetic.
cautions: Two pages handed on give different figures for the same thing: 85 on ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-329 and 50 on govinfo.gov/content/pkg/cfr-2026-title12-vol5/pdf/cfr-2026-title12-vol5-part329-subpartc.pdf. The first reads: "The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

question: Y147
answer:
SINGLE-COUNTERPARTY CREDIT LIMIT COMPLIANCE CALCULATION — 12 CFR Part 252, Subpart H, as in force 2026-11-21

1. RULE BASIS (text quoted from the eCFR pages fetched by the harness)

§ 252.70(a)(2)(i): 'Covered company means: (A) A global systemically important BHC; (B) A Category II bank holding company; and (C) A Category III bank holding company.'

§ 252.72(a) (General limit on aggregate net credit exposure): 'No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company.'

§ 252.72(b) (separate, narrower limit): 'No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company.'

§ 252.76(a)(1): 'If a covered company has an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital, the covered company must assess its relationship with the counterparty under paragraph (b)(2) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is economically interdependent with one or more other counterparties of the covered company and under paragraph (c)(1) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is connected by a control relationship with one or more other counterparties.'

§ 252.76(a)(2): if the assessment finds the (b)(2)/(c)(1) factors met (or the Board so determines under (d)), 'the covered company must aggregate its net credit exposure to the counterparties for all purposes under this subpart, including, but not limited to, § 252.72.'

2. INPUTS AND ASSUMPTIONS

Input A: Tier 1 capital of the covered company = $40,000,000,000.
Input B: Aggregate net credit exposure to a single counterparty = $11,000,000,000.
Assumptions (per project context, to be confirmed by the reporting entity, not re-derived here): (i) the company is a covered company under § 252.70(a)(2)(i) and the 25% general limit of § 252.72(a) is the applicable limit; (ii) $40B is tier 1 capital as measured for this purpose; (iii) $11B is the correctly measured aggregate net credit exposure under §§ 252.73–252.75 (gross exposure, eligible collateral/guarantee/credit-derivative recognition, SFT and derivative methodologies, SPV look-through); (iv) no exemption, carve-out, or affiliate-specific adjustment applies; (v) the counterparty is not a 'major counterparty' of a 'major covered company' (see § 6 caveat).

3. COMPUTATION

Step 1 — 25% cap (Ask 1).
Cap = 0.25 × Tier 1 capital = 0.25 × $40,000,000,000 = $10,000,000,000.

Step 2 — Excess over the cap (Ask 2).
Excess = Aggregate net credit exposure − Cap = $11,000,000,000 − $10,000,000,000 = $1,000,000,000.
Ratio checks: exposure/tier 1 capital = 11/40 = 27.5%; cap ratio = 25.0%; excess ratio = 1/40 = 2.5% of tier 1 capital. The exposure exceeds the cap; the company is in violation of § 252.72(a) by $1,000,000,000.

Step 3 — 5% assessment trigger (Ask 3).
Threshold = 0.05 × $40,000,000,000 = $2,000,000,000.
Test: is aggregate net credit exposure ($11,000,000,000) greater than the threshold ($2,000,000,000)? Yes — by $9,000,000,000; the exposure is 27.5% of tier 1 capital, 5.5× the 5% threshold.
VERDICT: TRIGGERED. The § 252.76(a)(1) obligation to assess the counterparty for economic interdependence (§ 252.76(b)(2) factors) and for control relationships (§ 252.76(c)(1)) is mandatory and self-executing on these numbers; it is not discretionary.
Important distinction: the trigger is the obligation to assess, not a finding of interdependence or control. Whether the counterparty is in fact economically interdependent or commonly controlled is a separate determination made by evaluating the § 252.76(b)(2) factors (e.g., ≥50% of gross revenue/expenditures between the counterparties; guarantees ≥50% of the company's net credit exposure) and the § 252.76(c)(1) control tests (≥25% of any class of voting securities; power to elect a majority of the board). If any factor is met — or the Board determines so under § 252.76(d) — the company must aggregate net credit exposure across the counterparties for all purposes under the subpart, including § 252.72, which would increase measured exposure and enlarge the § 252.72(a) violation computed above.

4. RESULTS (as reported)

Ask 1 — 25% exposure cap: $10,000,000,000 (USD).
Ask 2 — amount by which exposure exceeds the cap: $1,000,000,000 (USD).
Ask 3 — 5% economic-interdependence / control-relationship assessment triggered: YES (TRIGGERED).

5. WHY THE PROOF-OF-ABSENCE SEARCHES DO NOT PUT THESE ASKS IN not_stated

The harness searched the full text of https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-252.70 (2,645 chars), /section-252.72 (515 chars), /section-252.76 (7,920 chars), /part-252/subpart-H (58,488 chars), /part-252/subpart-Q (73,085 chars) and /chapter-II/part-252/subpart-H, and did not find the literal strings '$10 billion', '$10,000,000,000', '$1 billion', '$1,000,000,000', 'triggered', 'assessment required', etc. That absence is expected and is not an absence of the answer: Part 252 states a ratio (25 percent, 5 percent), not a pre-computed dollar amount for a hypothetical company, so no regulation could contain the string '$10 billion' for a $40B-capital company. The operative words are present and were quoted verbatim — '25 percent of the tier 1 capital' (§ 252.72(a)) and 'exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital ... must assess' (§ 252.76(a)(1)) — and the dollar results are arithmetic performed on the two inputs the request supplies. Accordingly the answer to each ask is not 'the page states none'; the pages state the governing ratios, and the figures are derived. not_stated is therefore empty, as is blocked_on.

6. COMPLIANCE CAVEATS AND LIMITS OF THIS CALCULATION

(a) 15% limit. If the company is a global systemically important BHC (hence a 'major covered company' under § 252.70(a)(2)(ii)) AND the counterparty is a 'major counterparty', the binding limit is § 252.72(b), not § 252.72(a): 0.15 × $40,000,000,000 = $6,000,000,000, and the excess over that limit would be $5,000,000,000. The answers above apply the 25% limit the request specifies; the category determination should be documented to confirm 25% is the operative cap.
(b) Category and applicability. § 252.70(c)(1)(i) set a July 1, 2020 compliance date for companies that were covered companies on October 5, 2018; § 252.70(c)(2) gives a company that becomes covered later until the first day of the ninth calendar quarter thereafter. Both are long past 2026-11-21 for any company covered since 2018, so Subpart H is in force; if the company became a covered company recently, confirm the § 252.70(c)(2) date has arrived.
(c) Exposure measurement. The $11B must be the aggregate net credit exposure computed under §§ 252.73–252.75 (gross exposure by transaction type; reductions for eligible collateral, eligible guarantees, eligible credit/equity derivatives and eligible guarantors; SFT and derivative methodologies; SPV look-through above the 0.25%-of-tier-1-capital threshold). If the $11B is a gross or unadjusted figure, the violation and the trigger verdict must be recomputed on the adjusted figure.
(d) Tier 1 capital measurement date. The quoted text of § 252.72 does not itself specify the measurement date; confirm against the § 252.71 definitions and the applicable FR Y-15 / FR Y-9C reporting instructions which quarter-end tier 1 capital figure governs, and that $40B is that figure.
(e) Rule currency. The eCFR pages were fetched 2026-11-23T00:13:20Z, two days after the 2026-11-21 as-of date; no amendment affecting the 25% or 5% figures appears in the quoted text, but a point-in-time (as-of 2026-11-21) eCFR or Federal Register check should be retained in the compliance file.
(f) Aggregation. Because the 5% trigger is met, the § 252.76 assessment must be performed and documented now; any affirmative finding aggregates exposures and can only worsen the § 252.72(a) position. Board determinations under § 252.76(d) or (e) (anti-evasion) could also compel aggregation.

7. CURE ARITHMETIC (for the remediation file)

To come into compliance with § 252.72(a) at the current capital level: reduce aggregate net credit exposure to at most $10,000,000,000, i.e. by at least $1,000,000,000.
Alternatively, to support $11,000,000,000 of exposure at exactly 25%: required tier 1 capital = $11,000,000,000 / 0.25 = $44,000,000,000 (an increase of $4,000,000,000). Note the limit is on exposure 'exceeding' 25%, so $44B of tier 1 capital with $11B of exposure sits exactly at, and does not exceed, the cap.
Note that curing the § 252.72(a) excess does not by itself extinguish the § 252.76 assessment obligation for a counterparty already over 5% at the time the obligation arose; document the assessment regardless.
cautions: The recompute vote reached no majority on ask 1, 2; that part of the answer was not compared.

Two pages handed on give different figures for the same thing: 2020 on ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-252.70 and 2022 on ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-252/subpart-q. The first reads: "(ii) Notwithstanding paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section, a company that is a major covered company as of October 5, 2018, must comply with the requirements of this subpart, including but not limited to § 252.72, beginning on January 1, 202"
The answer gives 1e+10 USD for ask 1, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.
The answer gives 1e+09 USD for ask 2, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.

question: Y148
answer:
REGULATORY DETERMINATION — 17 CFR 229.402(c) (Regulation S-K Item 402(c)), as in force 2026-11-21
Named executive officer with perquisites and personal benefits totalling $120,000, comprising (among others) one item of $24,000 and one item of $26,000.

=====================================================================
0. AUTHORITY RELIED ON AND VERSION CONTROL
=====================================================================
Primary text: 17 CFR 229.402, Item 402(c) (Summary Compensation Table) and its Instructions to Item 402(c)(2)(ix). Two independent renderings were read and agree verbatim on every operative figure:
  (a) eCFR 'current' — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-229/subpart-229.400/section-229.402 (fetched 2026-11-23T00:15:43Z; sha256 975472248ee6);
  (b) CFR 2025 print edition — https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol3/pdf/CFR-2025-title17-vol3-sec229-402.pdf (43 pp.; sha256 4c7154053e64).
Because the eCFR 'current' text fetched AFTER the stated effective date (2026-11-21) still carries the $10,000 / $25,000 / 10% figures, and the 2025 print edition carries the same figures, no amendment altered these thresholds between the 2025 revision and 2026-11-21.

Proposed-but-not-effective text noted and excluded: SEC Release No. 33-11455, Fact Sheet 'Executive Compensation Disclosure Reform' (Nov. 13, 2026) — https://www.sec.gov/files/33-11455-fact-sheet.pdf (sha256 4b44e3fa4e7f). It proposes to 'Update the minimum aggregate reporting threshold from $10,000 to $150,000 for each NEO' and to add a de minimis fringe exclusion. A proposal does not amend the CFR; it is not law on 2026-11-21. (This matters: see §6 trap analysis.)

=====================================================================
1. ASK 1 — MAY THE REGISTRANT EXCLUDE PERQUISITES ALTOGETHER?  ANSWER: NO.
=====================================================================
Operative text (quoted, Item 402(c)(2)(ix)(C) / Instructions to Item 402(c)(2)(ix), Instruction 4):
  'Perquisites and other personal benefits or property may be excluded only if the aggregate amount of such compensation will be less than $10,000.'
  'Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000.'
Application: aggregate = $120,000. $120,000 is not less than $10,000. The exclusion condition fails.
Consequences that follow automatically:
  (i)  The full $120,000 must be included in column (i) ('All Other Compensation') of the Summary Compensation Table. No de minimis or immateriality carve-out applies once the aggregate is at or above the floor.
  (ii) Each perquisite or personal benefit must be identified by type, 'regardless of its amount' — i.e. the $24,000 item and the $26,000 item must each be named/typed in the footnote even though only one of them is quantified.
  (iii) Valuation is at aggregate incremental cost to the registrant ('Perquisites and other personal benefits shall be valued on the basis of the aggregate incremental cost to the registrant').
  (iv) Tax reimbursements ('gross-ups') associated with perquisites must be separately identified and quantified as tax reimbursements under (c)(2)(ix)(B) irrespective of the $10,000 floor.
Verdict: NO — exclusion is not available; the $10,000 figure is an inclusion floor, not a disclosure exemption for this registrant.

=====================================================================
2. ASK 2 — WHAT IS THE FOOTNOTE QUANTIFICATION THRESHOLD?  ANSWER: THE GREATER OF $25,000 OR 10% OF THAT NEO'S TOTAL PERQUISITES — HERE $25,000.
=====================================================================
Operative text (Instruction 4 to Item 402(c)(2)(ix), quoted):
  'If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type. If perquisites and personal benefits are required to be reported for a named executive officer pursuant to this rule, then each perquisite or personal benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for that officer must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote.'
The threshold is therefore a two-pronged formula applied per officer:
  Threshold = MAX( $25,000 , 0.10 × TotalPerquisites(officer) )
Computation for this NEO:
  TotalPerquisites = $120,000
  10% prong      = 0.10 × $120,000 = $12,000
  Fixed prong    = $25,000
  Threshold      = MAX($25,000, $12,000) = $25,000   <-- the fixed prong binds
Operative footnote quantification threshold for this officer: $25,000.
Do NOT confuse the two numbers. The $10,000 figure is the aggregate inclusion/identification floor (Ask 1). The $25,000-or-10% figure is the quantification trigger (Ask 2). A separate, distinct $10,000 rule exists in Instruction 3 to Item 402(c)(2)(ix) and applies only to All Other Compensation items that are NOT perquisites or personal benefits ('Any item reported ... that is not a perquisite or personal benefit and whose value exceeds $10,000 must be identified and quantified in a footnote to column (i)').

=====================================================================
3. ASK 3 — WHICH OF THE TWO ITEMS MUST BE QUANTIFIED?  ANSWER: THE $26,000 ITEM ONLY.
=====================================================================
Apply the §2 threshold, item by item (a strict 'exceeds' test — an item exactly equal to the threshold is not quantified):
  Item A  $24,000  vs  $25,000  ->  $24,000 > $25,000 is FALSE  ->  identify by type; NOT quantified
  Item B  $26,000  vs  $25,000  ->  $26,000 > $25,000 is TRUE   ->  identify by type AND quantify in a footnote
Cross-check against the 10% prong as well: $26,000 > $12,000 (true) and $24,000 > $12,000 (true) — but the test is against the GREATER of the two prongs, i.e. $25,000, so the 10% comparison does not change the result. Both prongs must be cleared; here clearing $12,000 is irrelevant because $25,000 is the higher bar.
Result: only the $26,000 item must be quantified. The $24,000 item is not quantified but is NOT omitted — it is identified by type and is embedded in the $120,000 column (i) total.
For the quantified item the registrant must also 'describe in the footnote its methodology for computing the aggregate incremental cost.'

=====================================================================
4. DISCLOSURE PROCEDURE (step-by-step, executable)
=====================================================================
STEP 1  Determine the NEO population for the last completed fiscal year (PEO, PFO, and the next three most highly compensated). Run Steps 2-7 per NEO.
STEP 2  Identify every perquisite/personal benefit and value each at aggregate incremental cost to the registrant. Exclude items that are not perquisites by definition (e.g. items integrally and directly related to the performance of duties, and items furnished for the registrant's business purpose) — document each exclusion and its basis.
STEP 3  Sum all perquisites/personal benefits for the officer. If the sum < $10,000 -> may exclude entirely; STOP. If the sum >= $10,000 -> include the full sum in column (i) and proceed.
STEP 4  Identify EACH perquisite by type in a footnote to column (i), regardless of amount.
STEP 5  Compute Threshold = MAX($25,000, 0.10 × sum from Step 3).
STEP 6  Quantify in the footnote every item whose value EXCEEDS the Step 5 Threshold; describe the aggregate-incremental-cost methodology for each quantified item.
STEP 7  Separately: (a) quantify and identify tax reimbursements/gross-ups on perquisites as tax reimbursements under (c)(2)(ix)(B) regardless of any threshold; (b) for any All Other Compensation item that is NOT a perquisite or personal benefit, identify and quantify it if its value exceeds $10,000 (Instruction 3).

Pseudocode:
  total = sum(perq.value for perq in officer.perqs)
  if total < 10000: exclude_all()                       # Ask 1
  else:
      include_in_column_i(total)
      identify_by_type(all perqs)                      # regardless of amount
      threshold = max(25000, 0.10 * total)             # Ask 2
      for p in perqs:
          if p.value > threshold:                      # Ask 3, strict 'exceeds'
              quantify_in_footnote(p); describe_methodology(p)
      for item in all_other_comp if not is_perq(item):
          if item.value > 10000: identify_and_quantify(item)   # Instruction 3
      for tr in tax_reimbursements: identify_and_quantify(tr)  # (c)(2)(ix)(B)

=====================================================================
5. MODEL FOOTNOTE LANGUAGE (ready to adapt)
=====================================================================
'Column (i) — All Other Compensation (fiscal year 20XX) — [NEO].
Amounts in column (i) include perquisites and personal benefits with an aggregate incremental cost to the registrant of $120,000, consisting of: [type 1] — $__; [type 2] — $__; [type 3] — $__; [type 4] — $__; [type 5] — $__.
The item reported as [type N] was quantified at $26,000. Aggregate incremental cost for [type N] was computed as [methodology, e.g.: hours of personal use of company aircraft × hourly variable operating cost, plus crew travel and landing fees, net of any reimbursement by the executive]. Perquisites and other personal benefits are valued on the basis of aggregate incremental cost to the registrant.
The item reported as [type M] ($24,000) is identified by type but is not separately quantified because it does not exceed the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for this named executive officer ($12,000).'
Note on practice: identifying an item by type without quantifying it is what the rule requires below the threshold; voluntarily adding the amount is not prohibited but is unnecessary and is generally avoided so the footnote does not blur which items were quantified.

=====================================================================
6. TRAPS AND SENSITIVITIES (state explicitly so they are not misapplied)
=====================================================================
(a) $10,000 IS NOT THE QUANTIFICATION THRESHOLD. Answering '$10,000' for Ask 2 would be wrong; it is the aggregate inclusion floor. Any answer of '$5,000' is not supported anywhere in Item 402 — the full text of the eCFR page, the 2025 print CFR, the fact sheet and the 2011 archive contains no '$5,000', '5,000 dollars', 'quantification threshold', 'footnote threshold' or 'USD 5,000' string. The rule states '$25,000 or 10%' verbatim.
(b) THE 10% PRONG IS NOT ALWAYS DORMANT. It binds only when total perquisites ≥ $250,000 (10% of $250,000 = $25,000). Example: if this NEO's total were $300,000, the threshold would be $30,000 and NEITHER the $24,000 nor the $26,000 item would be quantified (both merely identified by type). At $120,000 the 10% prong ($12,000) is below the fixed prong, so $25,000 controls.
(c) THE 2026 PROPOSAL IS NOT LAW ON 2026-11-21. Under proposed Release 33-11455 the aggregate floor would become $150,000 and the $120,000 total would fall BELOW it, permitting complete exclusion and no itemization or quantification of either item. That is the wrong answer for a filing governed by Item 402(c) as in force on 2026-11-21; it becomes the right answer only if the amendments are adopted with an effective date on or before the relevant filing date. Monitor the adopting release.
(d) CHARACTERIZATION DRIVES THE RESULT. This determination assumes both items are perquisites or personal benefits. If either is instead a non-perquisite All Other Compensation item, Instruction 3 requires identification AND quantification of any such item exceeding $10,000 — in which case the $24,000 item would also have to be quantified. If either is a tax reimbursement/gross-up, it is separately quantified and identified as a tax reimbursement regardless of any threshold. Confirm characterization and incremental-cost valuation before finalizing.
(e) SMALLER REPORTING COMPANY. If the registrant is an SRC, Item 402(n) scaled disclosure governs; the $10,000 aggregate floor appears there as well, but the $25,000-or-10% quantification prong for SRCs should be confirmed against §229.402(n)(2)(ix) before relying on this memo. This analysis assumes a non-SRC filer. The Ask 1 verdict (no exclusion at a $120,000 aggregate) is unchanged either way.

=====================================================================
7. BOTTOM LINE
=====================================================================
1. No — perquisites may not be excluded: the $120,000 aggregate is not less than $10,000, so all perquisites go into column (i) and each is identified by type.
2. The footnote quantification threshold is the greater of $25,000 or 10% of that NEO's total perquisites; for a $120,000 total, 10% = $12,000, so the operative threshold is $25,000.
3. Only the $26,000 item must be quantified (and its aggregate-incremental-cost methodology described); the $24,000 item is identified by type but not quantified, and remains inside the $120,000 column (i) total.
cautions: The recompute vote did not run, so no figure in this answer was recomputed.
The answer gives 26000 USD for ask 3, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.

question: Y149
answer:
Compliance determination — OCC advanced approaches national bank, calendar year 2014.

Scope and governing rule
- Entity: national bank, advanced approaches, not a savings and loan holding company.
- Governing rule: 12 CFR Part 3 (OCC capital adequacy rules).
- Transition provision: 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A). The bank falls under §3.10(f)(1) because it is an advanced approaches national bank and is not an SLHC; §3.10(f)(2) addresses non-advanced banks and SLHCs.
- The provision states: 'From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent.'

Answer to Ask 1 — ratios applied Jan. 1 through Dec. 31, 2014
- Minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio: 4.0 percent.
- Minimum tier 1 capital ratio: 5.5 percent.
- Advanced approaches status does not change these flat minimum percentages. It affects the ratio calculation method (lower of standardized and advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets) and the timing of the supplementary leverage ratio, not the 2014 minimum percentages themselves. If the bank was on parallel run during 2014, risk-weighted assets may be calculated under the general risk-based capital rules and substituted for standardized total risk-weighted assets; the minimum percentages remain 4.0 percent and 5.5 percent.

Answer to Ask 2 — corresponding minimums in the reproduced 12 CFR Part 3 text
The reproduced 12 CFR 3.10(a) text states the general minimum ratios:
- 'A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.'
- 'A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.'
- 'A total capital ratio of 8 percent.'
- 'A leverage ratio of 4 percent.'
Therefore, the corresponding text minima are:
- Minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio: 4.5 percent.
- Minimum tier 1 capital ratio: 6.0 percent.
These are the fully effective minima in §3.10(a), not the 2014 transition in §3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A).

Comparison table
Ratio | 2014 transitional minimum applied | 12 CFR 3.10(a) text minimum
Common equity tier 1 | 4.0% | 4.5%
Tier 1 | 5.5% | 6.0%

Exclusions — Ask 3
- No capital conservation buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, GSIB surcharge, supplementary leverage ratio, tangible capital requirement, or other add-on is included in either result.
- Total capital (8 percent) and leverage (4 percent) are stated in the same transition paragraph only as context and are not part of the two requested ratios.

Source basis
- 12 CFR 3.10(f)(1)(iii)(A), 2014 CFR and current eCFR, and the 2024/2026 CFR Part 3 reproductions, all contain the same 2014 transition language.
- 12 CFR 3.10(a), 2014 CFR and current eCFR, contains the 4.5 percent CET1 and 6 percent tier 1 general minimums.
- 78 FR 62018 confirms the same 2014 transition: 'From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent...'

Conclusion
For Jan. 1 through Dec. 31, 2014, the applicable minimums for the advanced approaches national bank were 4.0 percent common equity tier 1 and 5.5 percent tier 1. The corresponding minimums in the reproduced 12 CFR Part 3 text are 4.5 percent common equity tier 1 and 6.0 percent tier 1.

question: Y150
answer:
CORPORATION TAX, NON-RING FENCE PROFITS, FROM 1 APRIL 2023 — HMRC RATES AND ALLOWANCES POSITION

SCOPE: standard (non-ring fence) UK Corporation Tax on the profits of companies, financial year 2023 (1 April 2023 – 31 March 2024) and each subsequent financial year through FY2026, as published in HMRC's 'Corporation Tax rates and allowances' guidance. Ring fence (oil and gas), Northern Ireland and special-rate entities are excluded except where flagged.

=====================================================================
1. ANSWER AT A GLANCE
=====================================================================

Ask 1 — Is there still a single Corporation Tax rate?
  NO. From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single rate for non-ring fence profits. (A single rate did apply for 1 April 2015 – 31 March 2023, at 19%.)

Ask 2 — Rate for profits of £50,000 or less
  19% — the small profits rate.

Ask 3 — Main rate for profits above £250,000
  25%.

Ask 4 — Profits between £50,000 and £250,000
  Taxed at the main rate of 25%, reduced by MARGINAL RELIEF. This produces a gradual increase in the effective rate from 19% at £50,000 to 25% at £250,000. Standard fraction 3/200.

=====================================================================
2. ASK 1 — THE SINGLE-RATE QUESTION (VERDICT: NO)
=====================================================================

HMRC's 'Corporation Tax rates and allowances' guidance states, in terms:

  "From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits."

and, in the rates table for the financial year 2023 (columns 2023–2026):

  Small profits rate (companies with profits under £50,000) .... 19%
  Main rate (companies with profits over £250,000) ............. 25%
  Main rate (all profits except ring fence profits) ............ — (blank from 2023; the single 19% rate appears only in the 2022 column)
  Marginal Relief lower limit ................................. £50,000
  Marginal Relief upper limit ................................. £250,000
  Standard fraction ........................................... 3/200

The publication's own change log records the switch: "21 December 2022 — From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits. Marginal relief is also available for companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000."

So the answer to ask 1 is a clear NO: two statutory rates plus a taper now apply, replacing the single 19% rate that applied for 1 April 2015 – 31 March 2023.

CAVEAT — SUPERSEDED ENTRY, DO NOT RELY ON IT: the same change log contains an earlier line, "3 October 2022 — The Corporation Tax main rate will remain at 19% from 1 April 2023." That reflected the position announced on 23 September 2022 and was reversed at the Autumn Statement on 17 November 2022; the 21 December 2022 entry and the current 2023–2026 rate columns supersede it. Any answer of 19% as the main rate from 1 April 2023 is wrong.

=====================================================================
3. ASK 2 — RATE FOR PROFITS OF £50,000 OR LESS (VALUE: 19%)
=====================================================================

Statutory name: the small profits rate (standard small profits rate, to distinguish it from the small ring fence profits rate at CTA10/s.279A).

Rate: 19%.

Sources, in HMRC's own words:
  - Rates and allowances table: "Small profits rate (companies with profits under £50,000) — 19%" for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026.
  - Rates guidance: "A small profits rate of 19% was also announced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less."
  - Marginal Relief guidance: "19% for taxable profits below £50,000 (small profit rate)".
  - Equality impact assessment: "A SPR has been reintroduced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less and these will continue to pay Corporation Tax at 19%."
  - CTM03905 confirms the reintroduction mechanism: "With effect from 1 April 2023, the standard small profits rate of Corporation Tax for non-ring fence profits has been reintroduced at CTA10/PART3A by FA2021/S6 and SCH1... Where the profits do not exceed a set lower limit, the total taxable profits are charged at a lower rate of CT, known as the standard small profits rate."

Precise condition: the test is applied to AUGMENTED profits, not taxable total profits alone (CTA10/s.18L: total taxable profits plus qualifying exempt distributions from unrelated, unassociated companies). If augmented profits are at or below the lower limit (L = £50,000, as adjusted), the whole of the taxable total profits is charged at 19%. If taxable total profits are nil or a loss, the rate is not engaged at all.

=====================================================================
4. ASK 3 — MAIN RATE FOR PROFITS ABOVE £250,000 (VALUE: 25%)
=====================================================================

Rate: 25%.

Sources, in HMRC's own words:
  - Rates and allowances table: "Main rate (companies with profits over £250,000) — 25%" for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026.
  - Rates guidance: "At the Spring Budget 2021, the Corporation Tax main rate for non-ring fence profits was increased to 25% for profits above £250,000."
  - Marginal Relief guidance: "25% for taxable profits above £250,000 (main rate)".
  - Equality impact assessment: "From 1 April 2023, the Corporation Tax main rate increased to 25% for profits of over £250,000."

Precise condition: 25% applies to the whole of the taxable total profits where augmented profits exceed the upper limit (U = £250,000, as adjusted). "Over £250,000" is strict; exactly £250,000 still falls within the marginal relief band (relief then computes to nil, so the effective rate is exactly 25% — see §5).

=====================================================================
5. ASK 4 — PROFITS BETWEEN £50,000 AND £250,000 (VERDICT: MAIN RATE REDUCED BY MARGINAL RELIEF)
=====================================================================

Treatment, in HMRC's own words:
  - "Companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate, reduced by a marginal relief. This provides a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate."
  - "Marginal Relief provides a gradual increase in Corporation Tax rate between the small profits rate and the main rate — this allows you to reduce your rate from the 25% main rate."
  - "Companies with profits of between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate of 25% which will be reduced by an amount of Marginal Relief (MR), providing for a gradual increase in the effective rate of Corporation Tax."

So the band is NOT a separate flat rate. It is 25% on the whole of the profits, less a marginal relief amount that shrinks to zero at £250,000.

5.1 THE CALCULATION (implementable procedure)

Definitions
  N = taxable total profits (the amount charged to Corporation Tax)
  A = augmented profits = N + qualifying exempt distributions from unrelated, unassociated companies
  L = lower limit = £50,000 (adjusted — see §6)
  U = upper limit = £250,000 (adjusted — see §6)
  F = standard fraction = 3/200 = 0.015

Algorithm
  Step 1. Compute N and A.
  Step 2. If A <= L:  tax = N x 0.19.  Stop.                     (small profits rate)
  Step 3. If A >= U:  tax = N x 0.25.  Stop.                     (main rate; MR = 0 at A = U)
  Step 4. Otherwise L < A < U:
            MR  = (U - A) x (N / A) x F
            tax = N x 0.25 - MR
          Where A = N (no exempt distributions), this simplifies to:
            MR  = (U - N) x F = (250,000 - N) x 0.015
            tax = 0.25 x N - 0.015 x (250,000 - N)
  Step 5. Effective rate = tax / N. By construction this lies in [19%, 25%].

Marginal effective rate inside the band: 25% + 1.5% = 26.5% on each additional pound between the limits (each extra £1 of profit is taxed at 25% and simultaneously loses 1.5p of relief).

5.2 WORKED TABLE (no associated companies, 12-month period, A = N)

  Profits N    25% charge    Marginal relief        Tax due      Effective rate
  £40,000      —              n/a (below L)         £7,600.00    19.000%
  £50,000      £12,500.00     £3,000.00             £9,500.00    19.000%
  £75,000      £18,750.00     £2,625.00             £16,125.00   21.500%
  £100,000     £25,000.00     £2,250.00             £22,750.00   22.750%
  £150,000     £37,500.00     £1,500.00             £36,000.00   24.000%
  £200,000     £50,000.00     £750.00               £49,250.00   24.625%
  £250,000     £62,500.00     £0.00                 £62,500.00   25.000%
  £300,000     £75,000.00     n/a (above U)         £75,000.00   25.000%

Checks: at N = £50,000 the formula gives MR = (250,000 - 50,000) x 0.015 = £3,000 and £12,500 - £3,000 = £9,500 = 19% of £50,000 — the band joins the small profits rate exactly. At N = £250,000 MR = 0 and the band joins the main rate exactly. No computed effective rate falls outside 19%–25%.

5.3 BOUNDARY CONVENTIONS TO IMPLEMENT EXACTLY
  - A <= £50,000 -> 19% (the guidance says 'under £50,000' in the table and '£50,000 or less' in the rates page and impact assessment; the statutory lower limit is inclusive, so £50,000 exactly is at the small profits rate).
  - A > £250,000 -> 25% flat ('over £250,000').
  - £50,000 < A <= £250,000 -> marginal relief band.

=====================================================================
6. THRESHOLD ADJUSTMENT — ASSOCIATED COMPANIES AND SHORT PERIODS
=====================================================================

The £50,000 and £250,000 limits are NOT always used at face value:

  "The lower and upper limits are proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and where there are associated companies." (Equality impact assessment)
  "The £50,000 and £250,000 profit thresholds are proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and by the total number of 'associated companies' your company has." (Rates guidance)

Implementation:
  adjusted limit = stated limit x (days in accounting period / 365) / (1 + number of associated companies)
Apply the same divisor to BOTH limits, then run the §5.1 algorithm with the adjusted L and U. The CT600 carries dedicated boxes for the marginal relief amount and the number of associated companies in the period.

=====================================================================
7. EXCLUSIONS AND ADJACENT RATES (stated so they are not confused with the above)
=====================================================================

  - Ring fence companies (oil extraction / oil rights, UK or UK continental shelf): separate regime. From 1 April 2023: small ring fence profits rate 19% (profits under £50,000), main ring fence profits rate 30% (profits over £250,000), ring fence fraction 11/400, with marginal relief between £50,000 and £250,000. For periods to 31 March 2023 the ring fence band was £300,000 – £1,500,000.
  - Unit trusts and open-ended investment companies: special rate 20% (2022–2026).
  - Accounting periods straddling 1 April 2023: time-apportion — the pre-1 April 2023 rate (single 19%) applies to the days before, and the new 19%/25%/marginal relief rules to the days from 1 April 2023.
  - Northern Ireland: not addressed in these passages; out of scope here.

=====================================================================
8. SOURCES RELIED ON
=====================================================================

  1. HMRC, 'Corporation Tax rates and allowances' (HTML guidance, updated 1 April 2026) — rate table, the 'no longer a single rate' statement, the 19%/25% sentences, the marginal relief description, the 3/200 standard fraction, the ring fence table.
  2. HMRC, 'Marginal Relief for Corporation Tax' — '19% for taxable profits below £50,000 (small profit rate); 25% for taxable profits above £250,000 (main rate)'; the gradual-increase description; the £50,000/£250,000 lower and upper limits.
  3. HMRC, 'Corporation Tax rates: Rates' (/corporation-tax-rates/rates) — 25% headline, small profits rate 19% for £50,000 or less, marginal relief between £50,000 and £250,000, proportionate reduction for short periods and associated companies, and the note that a single rate applied from 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2023.
  4. HMRC, 'Reintroduction of Corporation Tax Small Profits Rate and Marginal Relief — screening equality impact assessment' — 25% over £250,000, 19% at £50,000 or less, marginal relief between, and the proportionate reduction rule.
  5. HMRC Company Taxation Manual CTM03905 — statutory basis (CTA10/PART 3A, FA2021/s.6 and Sch.1), augmented profits definition (CTA10/s.18L), the lower-limit/upper-limit charging structure.

NOTE ON THE TWO PAGE-SCOPED ABSENCES: the harness recorded that CTM03905 does not print '19%' and that the publications landing page and CTM03905 do not print '25%'. Those absences are correct for those pages only — CTM03905 deliberately defers the figures to CTM03910, and the landing page is a document index. They do not bear on asks 2 and 3, because both figures are printed in terms on sources 1, 2, 3 and 4 above. Both asks are therefore answered with figures and neither is recorded as not stated.

=====================================================================
9. ONE-LINE ANSWER FOR DOWNSTREAM USE
=====================================================================

From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits: companies with profits of £50,000 or less pay the small profits rate of 19%; companies with profits above £250,000 pay the main rate of 25%; and companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 pay 25% reduced by marginal relief, giving a gradual increase in the effective rate from 19% to 25% (standard fraction 3/200; marginal effective rate 26.5% within the band; both limits proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and associated companies).
